title: From Time to Time
author: Jack Finney
target_audience: Adult readers interested in time travel stories
Fans of historical fiction set in New York
Readers who enjoyed 'Time and Again' by the same author
core_themes: The impact of individual actions on history
Nostalgia and the allure of the past
The tension between progress and tradition
The fragility and mutability of time
primary_purpose: To entertain readers with a suspenseful narrative that blends historical detail, romance, and philosophical reflection on the nature of time and consequence, while exploring how one person's choices might alter the course of history.

structure_format.organization: Linear, though structured around time travel episodes; primarily follows the protagonist’s journey through different eras
features: Rich descriptions of early 20th-century New York

key_concepts_lessons: Small actions can ripple through history in unpredictable ways.
Memory and longing can draw people powerfully toward the past.
The past is simultaneously enchanting and inhospitable for modern sensibilities.
Changing history, even with good intentions, can have unintended, far-reaching consequences.
Personal fulfillment may require sacrifices across time and relationships.
notable_features: Sequel to the beloved science fiction novel 'Time and Again'
Detailed recreation of historical New York City
Blend of realistic historical atmosphere and speculative time travel mechanics
Exploration of ethical dilemmas posed by time travel
cultural_historical_context: Published in 1995, 'From Time to Time' follows up on themes introduced in 'Time and Again' (1970), reflecting late 20th-century fascinations with nostalgia, the reliability of history, and the personal versus collective consequences of technological power.
reception_impact: Generally well-received by fans of the original novel for its nostalgic and atmospheric style
Praised for its meticulous research and immersive descriptions of historical New York
Some criticism for pacing and comparisons to the more tightly plotted 'Time and Again'
Maintains a cult following among fans of classic time travel fiction
comparable_titles: Time and Again by Jack Finney
The Time Traveler’s Wife by Audrey Niffenegger
Bid Time Return (Somewhere in Time) by Richard Matheson
